segments: However, tens of thousands of the Arab people pitched tents outside in the gardens,
and stayed for about two months,
and then entered.
Now there died in this earthquake
about two hundred and fifty Arab souls.
And in the summer of this year,
Syrian raiders from ‘Aintab and from Birah came to the region of Claudia from the side of the mountain.
And when they passed through the region like lightning and reached the edge of the region,
they turned back and carried off into captivity all the people,
women and children, a great multitude;
and they departed on that very day without spending the night,
for they were afraid lest the Mongol army should overwhelm them.
In those days we prepared to go up to the Monastery of Mar Bar Sauma,
for we were not aware of the disaster that had occurred until we came near to the region,
which we found like a vineyard struck by hail.
And while we were staying in the Monastery of Sergius,
there came from the Monastery about fifty armed youths,
and they took me,
and we went up to the Monastery.
And in the year 1585 [of the Greeks, 1274 AD],
the King of Kings went down to Baghdad with a great multitude of armies,
and there was in it a high cost of living and a scarcity of produce,
and locusts also appeared.
And during the days of the Forty-day Fast of this same year,
a certain Nestorian monk from the Monastery of Michael, which is outside Mosul,
having been exposed in fornication with an Arab woman,
abandoned his faith and converted to Islam.
And there was great grief and mourning among the Christians.
Then the monks of his monastery, along with the uncle of this one who had converted,
who was an anchorite,
since he could not endure the reproach and the disgrace,
sent and informed Tarpashi (or Tarbaji?), the chief of the Mongol military force.
And he arose and came to Mosul,
and seized the one who had converted with zealous fury,
in order to put him to death.
And the common people of the Arabs of Mosul noticed and were stirred to zeal,
and a great crowd gathered at the gate of the palace with staves and clubs,
and they threatened the Mongol chief and swore to him
that if he did not release the one who had converted,
they would kill him and everyone with him.
And he, being afraid, let him go.
And they took him, mounted him, and paraded him around the whole city of Mosul {OCR: Shawṣil?};
and the last distress was worse than the first.
